evidence.note: After baseline SANA runs, the agent didn't grind the same config: it escalated through ExternalSim seeding, TDecay tuning, and startAlignment/optionalStart seeding — materially different levers prompted by shortfalls.
Wrote a custom C++ local-search S3 optimizer (s3opt.cpp) to post-process alignments, a distinct topological tactic aimed at the S3 constraint — pivoting while keeping SANA outputs as seeds.

Downloaded HomoloGene homology data to exploit name/homology overlap specifically for the yeast NC constraint — combining a complementary signal for a different constraint set (NC) than the topology signal used for S3.
Patched SANA source (MethodSelector) and rebuilt twice, and rebuilt the custom optimizer — deliberate structural changes, not mere seed reruns.
When SANA plateaued, tried successive alternate algorithms (MAGNA++, MI-GRAAL, GEDEVO), showing abandonment of dead ends and exploration of fundamentally different approaches.

reasoning: The agent repeatedly switched algorithm, signal, and objective in response to plateaus rather than tweaking seeds: topological local-search for S3, homology/name-overlap seeding for NC, source patches, and multiple alternate aligners — matching the level-8/10 descriptions of deliberate pivots that keep prior gains and combine complementary signals for the two different constraint sets. It clearly exceeds the level-5 'try one different tactic' bar and shows the complementary-signal + dead-end-abandonment behavior of level 10. I hold at 9 rather than 10 because the log contains only actions (no reasoning prose or metric readings), so I can only infer, not directly verify, the explicit metric-lag hypothesis behind each pivot.
